test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13 Oct 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A 144-m-long wire of radius 4 mm is melted to form a sphere. What is the surface area (in cm²) of the sphere, assuming there is no wastage of material?
solution:
**Given**

length of wire = 144 m

radius of wire = 4 mm

**Formula used**

Surface area of sphere = 4πr²

Volume of wire = πr²h

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

1m = 100 cm

1cm = 10 mm

**calculation**

1m = 100 cm

144 m = 144 × 100

144 m = 14400 cm

Volume of wire = π(0.4)²14400

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

π(0.4)214400 = (4/3)πr³ 

⇒ r³ = (0.4 × 0.4 × 14400 × 3)/4

⇒ r³ = (0.4 × 0.4 × 3600 × 3)

⇒ r³ = (4/10) × (4/10) × (3600) × 3

⇒ r³ = (4 × 4 × 36 × 3)

⇒ r³ = (4 × 4 × 4 × 3 × 3 × 3 )

⇒ r = 4 × 3

⇒ r = 12

Surface area of sphere = 4 × π × (12)²

⇒ 576π cm²

**∴ Surface area of sphere is 576π cm² **
